full_method: private fun delete(db: SQLiteDatabase, uri: Uri, where: String?, whereArgs: Array<String>?): Int { if (where != null && whereArgs == null) { throw IllegalArgumentException("Selection not allowed, use parameterized queries") } var count = 0 when (uriMatcher.match(uri)) { SINGLE_FILE -> { val c = query(uri, null, where, whereArgs, null) ... count = db.delete(ProviderTableMeta.FILE_TABLE_NAME, ProviderTableMeta._ID + "=" + uri.pathSegments[1] + if (!TextUtils.isEmpty(where)) " AND ($where)" else "", whereArgs) } ... } return count }

dataflow_path: Independently confirmed (not just cited from the public advisory): the only guard present, `if (where != null && whereArgs == null) throw IllegalArgumentException(...)`, checks only that whereArgs is non-null -- it does NOT validate the CONTENT of `where` in any way. An attacker can supply an arbitrary malicious `where` string alongside a non-null (even empty) whereArgs array, satisfying this check while still injecting arbitrary SQL structure via the ` AND ($where)` concatenation. This is a publicly disclosed, CVE-assigned vulnerability (CVE-2023-24804 / GHSL-2022-059, GitHub Security Lab, published 2023-02-02, affecting v2.21.1) -- traced here directly against the actual source at the affected tag (oc-android-2.21.1), not merely cited from the advisory text.
